Water and air side heat balance review Using a similar validation method as described in the summer and winter data evaluation periods, we verified that the M&V data gives similar results for the heat transfer calculated using data for the air side and water side flows. The plots in Fig. 16 show very good alignment of the trends between the thermal power metrics for the CAV mode, with the calculated heat transfer for the air and water side flows differing by less than 5%. Very similar to what we observed with the previous data sets, there were larger discrepancies in the calculated heat transfer for the VAV mode, as shown in Fig. 17. This is expected, due to the changes in air flow rate through the coils for the VAV operating mode and the uncertainties of the air flow rate and air humidity measurements. These results provide confidence that the data measurements used to calculate the heat flows through the HEDS are reliable. 29 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Controllability As indicated in Table 10, the HVAC system was running with fixed setpoints, without automatically controlled and optimized dehumidification control during M&V operating periods 2 and 3 (VAV baseline and CAV baseline). The relative humidity (RH) at the zone level always remained less than 60% during the evaluation. To ensure that the RH is maintained within tolerances, the baseline operation without HEDS was controlled based on a fixed supply air setpoint of 50.5 °F. This is about halfway between the HEDS dynamically optimized dewpoint setpoint, which varied between approximately 49 °F and 52.5 °F during HEDS periods, as seen 30 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. in Fig. 18. As a result of the baseline operation utilizing fixed setpoints and not including the HEDS optimized dewpoint and supply air temperature setpoint logic, cooling loads delivered to the zones during the baseline periods were greater than during the HEDS operating periods even though the system controller indicates that no dehumidification is required.
